             Purpose:         This document establishes temporary guidelines for approval of fabricators in accordance
                              with the 2008 NYC Construction Codes.

       Related Code           AC     28-114.3               AC    28-116.7
         Section(s):          AC     28-116.2.3.1           BC    1704.2.2

 Related Buildings            BB     2011-008
       Bulletin(s):

           Subject(s):        Special inspections, fabricator approval; Approved fabricators, special inspections; Approved
                              fabricator, quality assurance agency; Certificate of Intent to Fabricate; Certificate of
                              Compliance


A. Background

     Sections BC 1704.2.2 and AC 28-116.2.3.1 exempt work performed on the premises of an approved fabricator
     from special inspections when the fabricator is approved by the Department. Sections AC 28-116.7 and BC
     1704.2.2 establish the basis for this approval. Section BC 1704.2.2 states:

                               Special inspections required by this code are not required where the work is done
                               on the premises of a fabricator registered and approved to perform such work
                               without special inspection. Approval of fabricators shall be based upon review of
                               the fabricator’s written procedural and quality control manuals and periodic
                               auditing of fabrication practices by an approved agency.

     The Department is in the process of promulgating a rule for the approval of fabricators. Until the rule is adopted,
     fabricators seeking temporary approval status shall follow the guidelines in this bulletin.

B. Compliance and Applicability.

     Design, fabrication, inspection and installation of fabricated items shall comply with the 2008 NYC Construction
     Codes and the guidelines listed in this bulletin. Section BC 1702 defines fabricated items as “Products and
     assemblies regulated by this code that are custom manufactured, or built prior to their incorporation into the work
     at the job site. Fabricated items shall not include listed, labeled or approved products or assemblies.”

C. Fabricators.

     1. Application – A fabricator must submit the following to the Office of Technical Certification and Research
        (OTCR) seeking temporary approval status:

               a. Certification from an OTCR-approved quality assurance agency issued to the fabricator, as well as
                  a copy of the signed contract between the fabricator and approved quality assurance agency and
                  any subsequent changes, amendments or modifications. An approved quality assurance agency
                  must meet the qualification requirements of section D of this bulletin.

               b. Quality control. A copy of the quality control manual, preferably in pdf format, and a list of all fabricator
                  employee titles participating in the quality control program, including a list of obligations,
                  responsibilities, authority and relevant certifications and experience for each title.

               c.   Proof of general liability insurance of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000.00) and, where
                    applicable, insurance required by the provisions of the New York State Workers’ Compensation and
                    disability benefits laws.

     2. Temporary approval – Temporary approval by the OTCR will be applicable only to the scope of work covered
        under the certification issued by the recognized quality assurance agency. Fabricators granted temporary
        approval can continue to be recognized as approved per this bulletin until a Department rule is promulgated.
        The Department retains the right to revoke this approval at any time.

     3. Duties and responsibilities

               a. Submitting construction documents in accordance with section E of this bulletin.

               b. Maintaining all records of inspection for a period of six years after submittal of the certificate of
                  compliance. Records shall be made available to the department upon request in accordance with
                  section AC 28-114.3.

D. Quality Assurance Agency.

     A quality assurance agency reviews fabricators’ written procedural and quality control manuals and performs
     periodic auditing of fabrication practices. A quality assurance certification agency provides certification for
     approved fabricators based on recommendations from the approved quality assurance agency. A single entity
     may serve simultaneously in both capacities.

     Until a Department rule has been promulgated, a quality assurance agency meeting the following requirements
     shall be considered for temporary approval. Required documents shall be submitted to OTCR for review and
     approval.

     1. Application

               a. Proof of accreditation. Submit documents from one of the options below:

                               i. Provide an ISO 17020 accreditation certificate from an accrediting body for the specific
                                  work covered under the fabricator’s responsibility. Accrediting body agencies shall be
                                  members of an internationally recognized cooperation of laboratory and inspection
                                  accreditation bodies subject to a mutual recognition agreement.

                              ii. Provide an accreditation certificate issued for a published quality assurance program
                                  (i.e., ISO 17021 or ISO 9001) by an accrediting body, along with the following:

                                          a) Fabrication type (i.e., steel, precast concrete, manufactured homes, etc.).
                                          b) Procedures for inspection and certification of the fabricator.

                                             OTCR will evaluate the documents submitted under sections (D)(1)(a)(ii)
                                             and (D)(1)(c) as proof of accreditation. If the qualifications are acceptable,
                                             the quality assurance agency will be provisionally recognized in accordance
                                             with the following:

                                             •     Provisional status will expire on January 1, 2012.
                                             •     The recognized agency shall diligently pursue accreditation to ISO
                                                   17020 prior to January 1, 2012.
               b. Statement of Independence. Membership-based organizations providing certification of approved
                  fabricators must subcontract all inspection and auditing functions with a separate, independent
                  accredited inspection agency. An independent inspection agency shall not engage in any activities
                  that may conflict with its objective judgment and integrity, including but not limited to having a financial
                  interest in the construction, installation, manufacture or maintenance of fabricated items it inspects.
                  The inspection agency shall submit a letter stating that it is independent of the membership-based
                  organization and has no financial interest in the fabricated items it inspects.

               c.   Identification of employees. For each quality assurance agency employee title participating in the
                    quality control program, provide a list of obligations, responsibilities, authority and relevant
                    certifications and experience.

      2.    Duties and responsibilities.

               a. Prepare and maintain inspection reports. In accordance with section AC 28-114.3, an approved
                  quality assurance agency shall maintain all records of evaluation and inspection for a period of six
                  years. Records shall be made available to the department upon request.

               b. Perform unannounced audits, at a minimum twice yearly.

               c.   For fabrication of manufactured housing, perform inspections of each factory-manufactured home as
                    per New York State Rules and Regulations (Title 19, Chapter XXXII, Part 1209), in addition to all
                    provisions contained herein.

E. Submittal of Construction Documents. The approved fabricator, approved quality assurance agency, and
   code required licensed contractor shall submit the following to the OTCR (280 Broadway, 7 th floor, New York, NY
   10007):

      1. Certificate of Intent to Fabricate. The approved fabricator, all applicable code required NYC licensed trades
         and (for manufactured homes only) registered design professionals shall submit the information contained in
         Attachment A, “Certificate of Intent to Fabricate Certificate of Compliance” within 2 weeks after the permit
         has been issued.

      2. Certificate of Compliance. The approved fabricator, all applicable code required NYC licensed trades and
         (for manufactured homes only) registered design professionals shall submit the information contained in
         Attachment A, “Certificate of Intent to Fabricate Certificate of Compliance” within 2 weeks after fabrication is
         completed.

      3. Prefabricated Assembly Evaluation Report. For all prefabricated construction assemblies having concealed
         work, the approved fabricator shall submit a prefabricated assembly evaluation report in accordance with
         sections FGC 107.1.2 and MC 107.1.2.

F. Installation of fabricated items
      1. Installation shall be in accordance with approved fabricators’ procedures.

      2. Installation in the field shall comply with all special inspection requirements of Chapter 17 and 1 RCNY 101-
         06.
